We enabled read replication for a Cloudflare D1 database used by a Worker. The current code still calls env.DB.prepare(...).run() directly. For checkout, a write is followed by a read in a later HTTP request, which currently carries no session context. The proposal is to use withSession("first-primary") for every request and describe the entire session as pinned to the primary; a teammate instead suggests withSession() always begins with the latest data. Checkout also batches a header insert and line-item inserts, and the team expects earlier statements to remain committed if a later statement fails.

Recommend a routing/session and failure-handling contract that supports useful replica reads without losing the checkout's prior write context. messages.reasoning_content:
Let me research Cloudflare D1 read replication documentation. Start with the supplied URL and follow links.

I should fetch:
1. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/
2. Read replication page: likely https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/ or https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/features/read-replication/
3. Sessions API: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#sessions or https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession
4. Batch: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/prepared-statements/#batch

Let me start.

Key facts so far:
- withSession() defaults to first-unconstrained = first query routed to any instance (primary or replica). Teammate's claim "withSession() always begins with the latest data" is wrong. It begins with unconstrained; sequential consistency afterwards.
- first-primary routes first query to primary, but session is not "pinned to primary" for all subsequent queries — subsequent reads may go to replicas with bookmarks ensuring at least as up-to-date. Actually the doc says "This approach is best when your application requires the latest database version." I should check the Worker API d1-database#withsession for exact wording on whether first-primary pins all queries to primary or only the first query.

Actually docs say "batched statements are SQL transactions" — if a statement fails, the whole batch is aborted and rolled back. That contradicts the team expectation that earlier statements remain committed. Let me verify.

Also the e-commerce tutorial might be useful: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/tutorials/using-read-replication-for-e-com

Let me fetch withsession and batch pages in parallel.
